question: Spike planted A Site Bind, 2v3, 33s. You are Viper (1 Snake Bite, Toxic Screen, Poison Cloud) toward A Long, teammate covers A Short. How do you hold post-plant?

options.label: Set a crossfire A Long / A Short with your teammate and save the Snake Bite for the defuse attempt
options.explication_courte: In a 2v3 the timer is your ally: two distinct angles force a trade, and saving the Snake Bite for the defuse moment is the highest-value use of your molly.

options.label: Deploy Toxic Screen to split A Site in two and isolate the A Long duels, save the molly
options.explication_courte: Cutting the site reduces sightlines and isolates duels in your favor, but in a 2v3 splitting the site may cede too much space too early.

sources_option.citation: Cutting the site or an approach with a wall isolates duels and forces defenders through a chokepoint, but overcommitting one side can open the opposite defuse angle.

options.label: Throw the Snake Bite onto the spike immediately to deny the defuse before the 3 DEF get organized
options.explication_courte: Throwing the molly before contact wastes it: it expires before the 3 DEF actually engage, and you lose your most valuable delay tool.

sources_option.citation: Use utility reactively and time mollies to the defuse; a molly thrown too early expires before the defenders actually commit, wasting your delay tool.

options.label: Rush A Short with your teammate to fish for a pick before the 3 DEF arrive grouped
options.explication_courte: Leaving post-plant to peek in a 2v3 hands the enemy a trade and frees the spike: you abandon your time advantage for a gamble.

sources_option.citation: As an attacker in post-plant you win by not donating a free duel and holding stable angles while the clock runs; pushing into a numbers disadvantage throws that away.

explication_longue:
Situation: 2v3 post-plant on A Site Bind, spike planted, 33 seconds. You are Viper with a Snake Bite, Toxic Screen, Poison Cloud; holding toward A Long, teammate covers A Short. Three DEF will retake.

In a 2v3 post-plant, time is your greatest ally: the defenders must defuse before detonation, so YOU hold all the leverage. Optimal play is patience: set a crossfire at two distinct angles (A Long and A Short), let the DEF come to you, force a trade, and save the Snake Bite for the exact moment a DEF touches the spike. The molly on the defuse is worth far more than an early throw.

Deploying Toxic Screen (acceptable) to split the site can isolate duels - but in a 2v3 it may cede space too early. Throwing the molly immediately before contact (costly) wastes it: it expires before the DEF engage. Rushing to fish for picks (mistake) abandons your post-plant leverage entirely.

Estimated elite distribution: ~54% crossfire + saved molly, ~22% Toxic Screen split, ~16% early molly (costly), ~6% rush for picks (mistake).

sources.citation: Attack post-plant means spreading out, playing off the spike, holding crossfires, and using utility to delay the defuse rather than dumping it early.
Crossfires are the most consistent ranked post-plant win condition; two players at distinct angles force a trade the defender can't isolate.
Prioritize time-stalling tactics over overcommitting to fights; in a post-plant the clock is your teammate, especially when outnumbered.
